purpose: Regenerate, from committed code, the Placement A forfeit numbers that audit/NUMBERS.md section 11 rows 50-54 book under the verification-run source class.  Discharges docs/OUTSTANDING.md O43; feeds docs/GATES.md G5.6.

free_choices.justification: The two forms the brief offers are the same function for b > 0.  Both satisfy condition (4) with equality at the boundary: at x = c*h(t) the clip argument is exactly 1 so r_t(x) = b >= b.  Checked on a grid in src/test_forfeit.py.
free_choices.consequence_if_wrong: A saturator that only approaches b asymptotically fails (4) and Proposition 2 would not apply even to the unsmoothed control.

free_choices.justification: The null scorecaster is legal (0 lies in [-b/2, b/2]) and reduces iteration (5) to pure error integration (8), the object Proposition 2 is stated about.  It isolates the smoother as the only manipulated variable.
free_choices.consequence_if_wrong: A non-trivial scorecaster shifts the level of the deployed threshold and therefore how often the adversary can sit on it; the forfeit would be measured against a different baseline.

free_choices.value: s_t = clip(q~_t, -b/2, +b/2); legality is Theorem 1's [-b/2, b/2]
free_choices.justification: The adversary plays the deployed threshold itself and falls back to the nearest legal value.  With q^ == 0 in [-b/2, b/2] and s in [-b/2, b/2], the reparameterised score s - q^ lies in [-b, b] and b/2 + b/2 = b is exactly tight.
free_choices.consequence_if_wrong: Reading legality as Proposition 2's [-b, b] lets the adversary match the saturated threshold +b exactly, destroying the induction's slack; the unsmoothed control then violates Proposition 2 too and stops being a control.  This is the zero-slack knife edge of research/S2/D1-reduction.json.

free_choices.value: err_t = 1{s_t >= q~_t}; a tie counts as a miscoverage
free_choices.justification: The paper writes a strict inequality.  BOTH readings give a non-degenerate experiment and they are near mirror images, so this is a real free choice: tie-to-adversary puts E_t's equilibrium at +0.5*h(t) and max|E_t| ~ 0.5*h(T) + (1-alpha); strict puts it at -0.5*h(t) and max|E_t| ~ 0.5*h(T) + alpha.  The tie reading is primary because an adversary that sets the score at the threshold intends to miss -- it is the limit of s_t = q~_t + eps as eps decreases to 0 -- whereas under the strict reading the adversary's signature move is a cover.  BOTH are run over every arm, as regimes `adversarial` and `adversarial_strict`.
free_choices.consequence_if_wrong: Every number in the primary regime changes by roughly (1 - 2*alpha) = 0.8 on max|E_t| for the tightly tracking arms; see the adversarial_strict rows for the exact size.  DISCLOSURE: the tie reading is also the one that reproduces S2's control numbers, and an earlier draft of this register justified it by claiming the strict reading was degenerate.  That claim was FALSE and this run disproved it.  The choice was made with S2's numbers already known and the reader is entitled to weigh that.

free_choices.value: gain_t = 1/(1 + t**p) on the new sample, p in {0.5, 0.9}
free_choices.justification: Equivalent to w_t = 1 - 1/(1 + t**p).  Gain 1/2 at t = 1 (a genuine average of the two available values) decaying as t**-p, so the effective time constant grows as t**p.
free_choices.consequence_if_wrong: gain = t**-p is singular at t = 1; 1/(c + t**p) adds a second free constant.  Either changes the head transient and, for p near 1, the measured excursion.

free_choices.value: q~_{t+1} = q_{t+1} - sign(u)*tau when |u| > tau, else q~_t
free_choices.justification: Algebraically identical to q~_t + S_tau(u), but in floating point it returns the target pulled back by exactly tau, so at tau = 0 it is bit-identical to the unsmoothed arm.  The additive form is not.
free_choices.consequence_if_wrong: Nothing in exact arithmetic; the degenerate-arm test would fail on representation.

free_choices.value: E_0 = 0, q_1 = 0, q~_1 = q_1; running mean seeded with q_1
free_choices.justification: q_1 = r_0(E_0) = 0 for every saturator satisfying F1; the smoother starts at the first output.
free_choices.consequence_if_wrong: A head transient of length O(1/(1-w)); irrelevant at the reported horizons.

free_choices.value: E_t = n_err_t - alpha*t with n_err an exact integer count
free_choices.justification: The accumulating form drifts by order 1e-11 over 10**6 steps; the counted form is exact to one rounding and keeps E on the exact 0.1 lattice alpha = 0.1 implies.
free_choices.consequence_if_wrong: No measurable change to any reported quantity.

free_choices.justification: Consumed only by the secondary open-loop regime.  The primary adversarial regime is fully deterministic and consumes no randomness.
free_choices.consequence_if_wrong: No effect on any primary number.

free_choices.value: i.i.d. uniform scores on [-b/2, b/2], shared bit-identically across arms
free_choices.justification: Not in the brief.  Added because the required CRN test -- every arm sees the identical score realisation -- is unsatisfiable by construction under a closed-loop adversary whose score is a function of the arm's own deployed threshold.  Doubles as a robustness column.
free_choices.consequence_if_wrong: The CRN test would have no referent and would have to be recorded as inapplicable.

dropped_tests.name: zero-cost invariance
dropped_tests.why_no_referent: It equates net growth with gross growth at a 0 bps cost level.  The re-scoped paper has no position, no growth column and no transaction-cost model, so this module defines no gross, net or cost_rate.  The quantities the test equates do not exist.

dropped_tests.name: cost identity
dropped_tests.why_no_referent: It asserts gross - net = cost_rate * turnover, where turnover is sum|pi_t - pi_{t-1}| over positions.  There is no decision priced in basis points in the re-scoped paper.  The nearest surviving quantity is deployed travel sum|q~_t - q~_{t-1}|, emitted per arm as `travel`, but it is not priced in anything and supports no identity.

aggregate_table_note: Derived from arms_raw[*].horizons_raw by derive_table(); recomputable without re-running the sweep.

regimes.adversarial: PRIMARY.  Closed loop: s_t = clip(q~_t, -b/2, +b/2), and a tie counts as a miscoverage (F4).  This is the regime whose numbers go in the paper.
regimes.adversarial_strict: SENSITIVITY on F4.  The same adversary with the paper's literal indicator err_t = 1{s_t > q~_t}.  Run over every arm so the size of the convention's effect is visible rather than asserted.
regimes.iid: SECONDARY (F10).  Open-loop seeded i.i.d. uniform scores on [-b/2, b/2], shared bit-identically across every arm.  Gives the CRN test a referent and shows which failures survive without an adversary.
